one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results, probably around Oct 22 (not yet confirmed; estimates run from Oct 15 to Oct 22). Guidance for Q3 was 750M lb copper at about $2.00/lb unit cost, and Q2 beat estimates but the stock fell, so the bar is the Grasberg ramp (65% in H2) plus a first 2027 volume outlook. There is also Section 232 refined-copper tariff news: the Sept 8 deadline passed without an announcement, and a report that the plan was losing momentum knocked Comex copper down 4.7% on Sept 10. A clean 'no tariff' outcome would squeeze the Comex premium, which hurts FCX's US-sold pounds. Copper is just off record highs ($6.56/lb Comex on Sept 30 against a $6.83 record on Sept 22). Both effects roughly cancel, so I centre slightly below spot (median about $70.2) with monthly vol of about 14% (48%/3.5), plus a small tilt for the earnings-day event. The window has two-sided event risk but no directional edge.

fair_value.method: Two methods at a skeptical long-run copper deck of $5.75/lb (below $6.56 spot) with gold at $4,000/oz. First, 2027E EPS of about $4.00 times 16x = $64. Second, 2027E EBITDA of $15.5B times 7.0x, less about $4B net debt and about $24B minority interests (PTFI and Cerro Verde), over 1.44B shares = $56. Equal-weight blend is about $60.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027E EPS $4.00 (copper $5.75, gold $4,000, ~3.6B lb Cu sales) x 16x

inputs_detail.derivation: EBITDA $15.5B - DD&A ~$2.4B - interest ~$0.3B = $12.8B pretax; 30% tax (2026 guided ETR) = $9.0B; ~35% to noncontrolling interests (PTFI 51% Indonesia, Cerro Verde minorities) = $5.8B / 1.44B shares. Close to the consensus of $4.13-4.23.

A discount to FCX's usual high-teens/20x forward multiple, because 2027 earnings rest on near-record copper that bank decks (Goldman 2027 $10,750/t) and ICSG's 377kt 2027 surplus say is above mid-cycle. Morgan Stanley's $66 target implies a similar multiple.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E EBITDA $15.5B x 7.0x = $108.5B EV; less net debt ~$4B (incl. smelter debt), less NCI ~$24B; /1.44B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 3.1B lb guided for 2026. Grasberg reaches 80% by mid-2027 and near full by end-2027, so 2027 is only partly recovered. I haircut toward MS's 'late 2027 recovery' view.

Spot is $6.56 Comex, partly a tariff-arbitrage artifact. Goldman's 2027 view is $10,750/t (~$4.90/lb) and Citi's is $15,000/t (~$6.80). I skew below spot because of the ICSG surplus and the 1M+ t US stock overhang if the tariff is dropped.

Q2 2026 operating EBITDA was ~$2.5B at a $6.17 realized price and 786M lb. Scaled to 3.6B lb at $5.75 with a unit cost of about $1.75-1.90, gold ~1.1-1.2Moz at $4,000, and sensitivity of $150M per $0.10/lb copper.
The historical mid-cycle range for large diversified copper miners is about 6-8x. Resource-nationalism and Indonesia jurisdiction risk argue against a premium.

inputs_detail.value: $2.1B ex-downstream; ~$4B incl. PTFI smelter debt ($9.4B debt - $4.1B cash, plus target range $3-4B)

inputs_detail.derivation: PTFI is 51% held by Indonesia (FCX 48.76%, falling to ~37% from 2042 under the MOU), plus Cerro Verde minorities. I value this at about 1.3x book NCI, consistent with ~35% of earnings going to minorities.

bear.story: The Section 232 refined-copper tariff is abandoned or delayed. The 1M+ t US stock overhang unwinds, Comex falls to LME and LME retraces toward Goldman's ~$11,000/t as the ICSG 2027 surplus shows up. FCX earns ~$2.60 EPS at ~$4.90 copper. A second Grasberg hiccup (wet ore, ore-loading modifications) or Indonesian fiscal demands tied to the IUPK extension pushes recovery into 2028. About 16x trough earnings gives ~$42, near the 52-week low area of $35-45.

base.story: Copper eases to $5.75-6.00 from record highs. Grasberg hits 80% by mid-2027 roughly on schedule, and 2027E EPS is ~$4.0-4.3. The stock trades at 15-16x forward EPS, roughly where it is now, minus some multiple compression as the cycle ages.

bull.story: Copper holds above $6.50 (Citi's $15,000/t supply-deficit view). The tariff is enacted, which keeps the Comex premium on US output. Grasberg is at full rate by late 2027, 2028E EPS is $5.5+, and variable dividends and buybacks rise. About 17x gives ~$95.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$48 (about 32% down, 0.7 sigma of a year's vol, but below the April guidance-cut low of ~$61 and the $58.50 lowest street target), the market would be pricing copper back near $5 or a real impairment to Grasberg economics: another block-cave incident, or IUPK extension terms that take a larger share. That would be more than a copper-beta pullback.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results; Grasberg ramp vs 65% H2 target; first 2027 outlook
US Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision (deadline missed Sept 8; phased duty proposed from Jan 1, 2027)
Q4 2026 results and formal 2027 volume/cost/capex guidance
Indonesia IUPK extension beyond 2041 (application June 2026); terms of the ~12% stake transfer and fiscal conditions
Grasberg Block Cave expected at ~80% capacity
Securities class action over Grasberg safety disclosures (Feb 2022-Sept 2025 class period)

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: spot $6.56/lb is near a record and partly a tariff-arbitrage artifact; ICSG sees a 377kt 2027 surplus
Whether the US refined-copper tariff is enacted (supports the Comex premium on FCX's US sales) or dropped (inventory overhang unwinds)
Grasberg Block Cave ramp: already slipped once (85% to 65% H2 2026 target), with wet-ore and ore-loading constraints
Indonesia jurisdiction: IUPK extension terms, stake dilution to ~37% from 2042, export and smelter rules
Insider selling: Chairman sold ~$25M in Feb 2026, and the General Counsel sold $6.3M on Aug 25, 2026 near highs
reasoning: Research focused on the bear case. (1) Execution: Grasberg's post-mud-rush ramp already cut 2026 copper guidance from 3.4B to 3.1B lb and gold from 0.8M to 0.65M oz. MS downgraded to EW ($66), and Q1 10-Q disclosures say PB2/3 are capped near 60% until ore-loading changes. (2) Copper: Comex hit a record $6.83 on Sept 22 but is partly tariff-driven. The Sept 8 Section 232 deadline passed with no announcement, Comex fell 4.7% in a day on reports the plan was losing momentum, over 1M t of metal sits in the US, and ICSG forecasts a 377kt 2027 surplus. Goldman's 2027 deck is about $10,750/t, well below spot. (3) Governance and legal: a securities class action is pending, and insiders sold into strength (Chairman ~$25M in Feb, GC $6.3M in Aug). (4) Balance sheet is not a bear point: net debt of $2.1B is below the $3-4B target, so there is no credit stress. Weighing this honestly: the stock's 98% one-year run already prices much of the copper upside. Consensus 2027 EPS of ~$4.1-4.2 at 16-17x gives $66-71, near spot. My fair value is $60 at a $5.75 deck, but spot copper above $6.5 is a real bull offset, and the balance sheet removes much of the tail-risk. So I set the 12-month median at ~$67 (slightly below the $70.58 close) with a lognormal-ish spread of sigma ~0.43, a bit below the 48% realized vol but wide for a copper-beta name, and a slightly fattened left tail. Scenario mean is about $67. Research was limited to about 10 searches and fetches, and X/Twitter was not attempted.
